title: Reviewing an Optional Customer Name
situation: You are reviewing a small Python function that formats a customer name for an internal support dashboard.

options.text: The function can raise an attribute error when either name value is missing.
The local variable names are too descriptive for a short function.
The function must use a loop before joining the two name values.
The function needs to write the formatted name back to the database.

guidance: Consider what customer.get returns when a key is absent.
Check whether every returned value supports the method called on it.

what_worked_well: You traced how missing input moves through the function.
areas_to_consider: Consider how a default value or explicit validation could make the behaviour predictable.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Tracing optional values helps identify runtime risks before they reach users.

what_worked_well: You considered readability and future maintenance.
areas_to_consider: Also trace the possible values returned by each dictionary lookup.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Understanding dictionary defaults and string methods supports safer Python code.

what_worked_well: You considered alternative ways to assemble the displayed value.
areas_to_consider: Focus first on whether the values are always strings before changing the assembly approach.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Reviewing value types helps select an appropriate implementation.

what_worked_well: You considered how the formatted value might be used elsewhere.
areas_to_consider: Keep the review focused on the function's stated display purpose and its immediate runtime behaviour.

skill_to_explore.why_relevant: Following the function's actual execution path helps prioritise the issue present in the snippet.
